items.note: In all three samples the focused filter field is a rounded input with a 2px blue focus border, a clear × and a live result count, following the system's input recipe. The first screen keeps the system's look: four saturated stat tiles with cream spot plates, cream panels and ink pills. In sample 3 a tile's delta caption wraps and leaves its arrow hanging, and the figures stay about 32px, where the reference's colour tiles (08) let one huge number carry the tile.

The night version is convincing: a navy page, indigo panels, white pills with ink labels, and the focused filter ringed in the night focus colour. It reads like the reference's night band (03), and the field hues of the stat tiles hold on the dark ground.

On phones the search pill, the ink Search pill and the avatar circle sit in a compact white top bar, and the focused filter keeps its blue 2px border. The four stat tiles stack as full-width saturated blocks, so about one and a half screens of solid colour come before any panel. In the reference, a field is one statement per view.

The table itself is in the language: cream frame, 1px rules, status pills with dots, cream circle row actions. But the hovered row looks the same as its neighbours in all three samples. Nothing is designed for this state, while the reference gives every interactive element a visible state (11).
The night table is well toned, with indigo rows, links on navy and dark circle chevrons. Still, no row shows a hover tone in any sample, so the pointer state cannot be seen.

On phones the table scrolls inside its cream frame with columns cut at the edge, as the spec intends. No row looks different from the others, and the filter pills wrap so that one pill sits alone on a second line.

The focused sidebar item gets a rounded blue ring that follows the pill shape: offset on the cream pill in samples 2 and 3, and flush on the ink pill in sample 1. This is close to the reference's ring on its ink pill (11).
At night the focused nav pill gets a yellow rounded ring, offset from the pill, that is easy to see on indigo. This is the system's on-field ring, applied consistently.

On phones the focus lands on the menu circle (sample 1) or the search pill (samples 2 and 3), shown with a blue border or ring that is clearly visible and rounded. The page below is the same stack of saturated tiles as the other phone states.

The account pill opens a white menu with rounded corners and a float shadow: the email as a quiet header, then three plain items, with a flipped chevron on the trigger. It is clean and sits squarely in the system. It is plainer than the reference's pill-led controls, but nothing is off.
At night the menu turns indigo with white bold items and sits on the navy page without a heavy border, which is consistent with the derived night palette.
On phones the same white floating menu drops from the avatar circle and covers the greeting cleanly. The items are readable and the menu stays within the screen edge.

Sample 3 does it well: a large magnifier composition with crescent shading, a sparkle, a bold title, one line and an ink pill. Sample 1 has only a lone ring-and-dot glyph above the text. Sample 2 is a blue panel with its text pushed right of an empty half and no drawing. The reference's spot art (07) always pictures something.

The dark versions repeat the light ones: the magnifier composition holds up on indigo in sample 3, sample 1 is a small ring glyph, and sample 2 is a blue panel with a blank space where the art should be.

On phones sample 3 keeps its magnifier composition above the title and the ink pill. Sample 1 has the small ring. Sample 2's blue panel starts with a tall empty band before the text, so the state reads as unfinished.

The stat tiles become cream skeleton cards with rounded bars and visible 'Loading' text, and the refresh pill keeps its width while showing pop-dots. This follows the system's loading recipe. Data panels that are already loaded stay put.

The skeletons turn indigo and the white pill shows pop-dots, which is consistent with the night palette. In samples 1 and 3 the footer's bottom strip turns bright white at night and breaks the navy page.
On phones the refresh pill shows pop-dots next to a 'Loading' line with its own three dots, above full-width cream skeleton cards. It is calm and clear, and in the system's language.

The stat-tile plates hold small flat pictograms that each read as their subject: a rocket, a sun over a hill, a storm cloud or bell, a clock. Each has a sparkle, and the shading is light. They are smaller and simpler than the reference's spot pictograms (07). The greeting moon with its sparkle is a neat breathing glyph, and the initials avatars are plain discs in one hue.

All three samples draw the header-band cluster almost exactly like the spec's example: a yellow hexagon with a side shade, a tilted pill (orange or pink), a large white star and a small sparkle. It is well made but pictures nothing about the area, and the three samples are near copies of each other. The reference's hero art (02) is a scene chosen for its subject.
The detail page reuses the same hexagon-and-pill cluster as the list page in every sample. Only sample 2 adds a subject plate, a stack of pill 'servers', which is a good, readable pictogram.

Each sample builds its own team cluster with crescent shading and two sparkle sizes: a sun behind a cloud, a pink blob with a yellow disc, an orange disc with a cloud. These are varied and to the recipe, though they show a mood rather than a team.

The motion follows the spec. The greeting moon breathes slowly, the header-band cluster drifts a few pixels over 8s, stat plates fade in once, and a detail plate builds in. Nothing bounces, and data stays still, which matches the calm, slow motion the spec describes.

findings.summary: The no-results empty state gets the system's composition in only one sample. Sample 1 shows a lone ring-and-dot glyph. Sample 2 is a full blue panel whose art area is blank: an empty left half on desktop and an empty top band on phones. The reference's spot art (07) always draws a readable subject. The spec allows a glyph as a substitute and lists 'a dot in a ring' among its glyphs, so agents can meet the rule with a ring.
findings.promptFix: Every empty state draws one `size.art` shape-kit composition of what is missing (for a search or filter with no results, a magnifier, an empty tray, a cloud with nothing under it), built from 2–3 crescent-shaded primitives plus a sparkle. A glyph is never the empty state's only art; dot-in-ring, discs and dots are accents. Draw the composition in hues different from the panel it sits on, so no piece disappears into the ground, and centre the text and pill beneath it. Never leave the art column empty.
findings.specRule: Empty state | Panel in the area hue …, one `size.art` shape-kit composition of the area's subject or a `size.glyphLg` glyph

findings.summary: Clickable table rows show no hover tone in any sample, although the spec specifies `color.surface.subtle`. The hover screenshot cannot be told apart from rest, while the reference designs a visible state for everything you can press. This has been open since rc.2.

In all three samples the projects-area header cluster is the spec's example cluster almost exactly: a yellow hexagon, a tilted pill, a large star and a small sparkle. The detail page reuses it. It is well made but pictures nothing about the area, and the three runs are near-identical. The reference's hero art (02) is a scene chosen for its subject.
findings.promptFix: Mark the sample cluster as a structure only: never reuse its exact shapes. Each area's lead shape comes from a noun for that area's subject, and a detail screen's cluster adds or swaps one piece that names the item's kind.
findings.specRule: <!-- Header-band cluster, one of many: lead hexagon, overlapping pill, large star + small sparkle --> <svg viewBox="0 0 240 200">

findings.summary: On phones the four stat tiles stack as full-width saturated blocks. About one and a half screens of solid colour come before any other panel, so the first screens are several large fields in a row. The reference treats a field as one statement per view (08 on desktop is a single row). The spec's one-column rule for card grids below the breakpoint leads to this.
findings.promptFix: On phones, stat tiles stay a 2×2 grid (or a horizontal scroll row) of compact tiles with the plate dropped, never four full-width saturated blocks stacked.
findings.specRule: Below `breakpoint.md`: … card grids to one column (two below `breakpoint.lg`)

findings.summary: Stat-tile figures stay about 32px. In sample 3 the delta caption wraps and leaves its arrow hanging beside two lines. In the reference's colour tiles (08), one huge bold number carries the tile. The spec still sets the stat number at `font.size.h3`.
In dark mode the footer's bottom bar turns into a bright white strip under the navy page.
